title: dedicated-poc-gpu-tco-scenarios-and-runbooks
summary: Workshop notes and concrete capacity/TCO scenarios for a mid-market customer POC. Includes workload assumptions, three sizing scenarios, autoscale/runbook recommendations, warm-pool strategy, and cost math for A100/H100 options.
body:
Executive summary:

This doc captures outputs from the 2025-11-21 solutions-eng workshop for a mid-market POC (customer X) exploring Redwood Dedicated capacity. Goal: recommend a set of realistic capacity footprints and autoscaling policies that meet a 95th percentile latency SLO of 250ms for interactive chat use cases while keeping monthly GPU spend within the customer’s guidance (~$25k/mo) where possible.

Customer context and constraints:
- Product: customer X chat assistant with short to medium context (512–2048 tokens). Typical request size 256 tokens in/out.
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn text generation.
- Expected concurrency (initial POC): peak 35 concurrent active sessions, average 12. Bursty traffic with hourly peaks and regular morning spike.
- Data controls: customer requires VPC/private deployment; no shared cache with hosted.
- Budget target for POC: $20k–$30k USD per month for infra.
- Acceptance criteria: stability under 2x expected peak for 72 hours and quantifiable cost estimates.

Workload profile and assumptions used for sizing math:
- Model family: 7B–13B class transformer. Latency dominated by forward pass; KV cache used for multi-turn.
- Typical request length: prompt 150 tokens, generation 100 tokens average.
- Effective tokens per request: 250 tokens.
- Server-side batching enabled (continuous batching) with max batch size tuned per GPU.
- Target throughput per GPU based on benchmarks (internal perf table):
  - A100 80GB: ~95–120 tokens/sec for 13B single-stream throughput when optimized, supporting ~0.38–0.48 reqs/sec at 250 tokens per request (approx).
  - H100 80GB: ~140–170 tokens/sec -> ~0.56–0.68 reqs/sec.
  - Ampere 40GB-class (dense): lower throughput and fits only trimmed models; not preferred given latency SLO.
- We plan to pin model version (no multi-model routing for POC).

Sizing methodology (how we translate concurrency to GPUs):
1) Convert concurrency to required RPS assuming average think time and active request duration. For interactive sessions, assume average user think time of 30s: concurrency-to-RPS factor ~1/30. For conservative sizing we instead use observed request duration driven by server processing: derive RPS = concurrency * requests_per_session_per_sec.
2) Use tokens/sec per GPU -> multiply by average tokens per request to get reqs/sec per GPU.
3) Apply headroom factor (1.25x for burst tolerance) and additional buffer for autoscale cooldowns.

Three recommended scenarios (conservative to aggressive)
Scenario A — Cost-savvy (goal: < $30k/mo):
- Hardware: 3 x H100 80GB nodes (shared across model shards).
- Assumed per-node usable throughput: 1.8 reqs/sec (conservative). Total peak capacity: 5.4 reqs/sec -> supports ~194 concurrent active sessions under our session model.
- Cost estimate (public list-equivalent): H100 instance ~$9.50/hr -> 3 nodes = $28.5/hr -> ~$20.5k/mo (24/7). + network/storage ~ $1.5k/mo -> estimated $22k/mo.
- Autoscale policy: min 2 nodes warm, scale to 3 on sustained 70% utilization over 90s, scale down to 2 after 10m idle. Warm pool: 1 node pre-warmed.
- Pros: hits budget target, robust for POC. Cons: limited headroom for unexpected growth.

Scenario B — Balanced (recommended default for POC):
- Hardware: 4 x A100 80GB (cost/perf sweet spot for 13B models in our perf matrix).
- Per-node usable throughput: 1.1 reqs/sec -> total 4.4 reqs/sec -> supports ~160 concurrent sessions.
- Cost estimate: A100 ~$5.75/hr -> 4 nodes = $23/hr -> ~$16.6k/mo. + ops/network $1.8k/mo -> ~ $18.4k/mo. Consider reserved contract reduces effective cost 25–30%.
- Autoscale: min 2 nodes, scale steps +1 node at 65% sustained util for 60s, cooldown 7m, burst mode allows temporary 50% overcommit for 15s via request queueing and lower batch targets to keep latency.
- Pros: better throughput headroom with lower ~$ cost. Cons: potential higher memory pressure for context; needs quantization checks.

Scenario C — High-headroom (latency-first):
- Hardware: 5 x H100 80GB (fastest single-stream).
- Per-node usable throughput: 1.6 reqs/sec -> total 8 reqs/sec -> supports ~288 concurrent sessions.
- Cost estimate: 5 * $9.5/hr = $47.5/hr -> ~$34k/mo + $2k ops -> ~$36k/mo.
- Autoscale: min 3 nodes warm, scale up to 5 at 60% util sustained 45s, scale down after 5m idle. Warm pool: 2 nodes.
- Pros: comfortable headroom for spikes, meets aggressive latency targets. Cons: cost above stated POC budget.

Autoscaling policy details and runbook
- Metrics to drive scaling: aggregate GPU token throughput, 99th percentile batch latency, pending request queue length. Use token throughput because it normalizes across request sizes.
- Primary rule set (example):
  - Scale up +1 node when average GPU util > 70% for 45–90s and pending queue > 10 requests.
  - Scale down -1 node when average GPU util < 35% for 7m and pending queue = 0.
  - Emergency scale-up: on queue growth > 50 requests or sustained tail latency > 800ms -> immediate +2 nodes with alert to on-call.
- Warm pool and pre-warming: keep a 1–2 node warm pool depending on scenario. Warm pool nodes should be kept with model loaded and KV cache empty to reduce spin-up time to ~30–60s. Warm pool financing impacts cost; include in TCO.
- Preflight sequence for scale events:
  1) Autoscaler triggers provisioning request.
  2) Orchestrator spins up VM and injector deploys model artifact.
  3) Health probe verifies model inference path (< 100ms cold single-token pass).
  4) Node joins router and begins receiving traffic.

Runbook highlights (for SRE during POC):
- If p95 latency breaches 350ms for >10m: check batch size drift, KV cache hit rate, and GPU memory pressure. If batch sizes are dropping unexpectedly, route-fallback to smaller-batch config or increase node count.
- If autoscaler unable to provision: fallback to hosted api route (fail-open) per customer agreement; notify SE and infra on-call.
- If cost forecast exceeds 20% of target: trigger weekly review and consider temporarily reducing min nodes or lowering model quality (quantized variant).

Cost math examples (simplified)
- Example: Scenario B (4x A100) baseline. 4 nodes * $5.75/hr = $23/hr -> monthly = $23 * 24 * 30 = $16,560. Add 12% overhead for storage/network/control plane -> $18,587. Round to $18.6k/mo. If reserved commit negotiated at 30% discount -> $13k/mo.
- Example per-request delta: At 4.4 reqs/sec sustained -> ~380k reqs/day -> 11.4M reqs/mo. If customer wants per-request cost estimate for internal chargeback, divide TCO by monthly requests -> ~$0.0016/req at $18.6k/mo.

Performance tuning levers to reduce TCO and improve latency
- Aggressive quantization (4-bit where safe) to increase batch capacity per GPU and reduce memory footprint. Must validate quality on customer prompt set.
- Prefix/KV cache warming for expected repeat contexts to avoid repeated prompt evaling. For private deployment, we can enable per-tenant cache.
- Dynamic batch target tuning: reduce target batch size under 95th percentile latency pressure to reclaim p95.
- Hybrid routing: use cheaper A100 nodes for background/low-priority reranks and reserve H100 for interactive generation.

Open questions documented from workshop
- Customer data retention and KV cache lifecycle: how many sessions are expected to be cache-hot and for how long? (action: SE to get usage traces)
- Can customer accept a brief warm-up window (30–60s) for new nodes or require near-instant scale?
- Preferences on reserved vs on-demand pricing (they indicated interest in 6–12 month commitment if unit costs drop 20-30%).

Decisions made during workshop
- Proceed with Scenario B as default for initial 4-week POC with a safety net to increase to Scenario A or C if acceptance tests demand it.
- Add one additional week of performance profiling during POC week 1 to collect token distribution and KV hit rates.

Next steps and owner matrix
- SE (Sofia Patel) to produce a short perf-testing harness and schedule profiling window (due 2025-11-10) [done].
- Infra (Liam O'Connor) to provision a staging cluster with 2 A100 nodes and warm-pool setup (due 2025-11-14).
- Customer-eng (Priya Singh) to gather sample traffic traces and confirm cold start constraints (due 2025-11-07).
- Finance (Ethan Morales) to draft a 30-day TCO estimate and create reservation proposal (due 2025-11-18).

Appendix: quick calculation worksheet (for SEs)
- tokens_per_request = 250
- target_p95_latency_ms = 250
- tokens_per_gpu_sec (A100) = 110 (median) -> reqs_per_gpu_sec = 110/250 = 0.44 -> reqs_per_gpu_hour ~ 1584 -> monthly ~ 1.14M reqs
- headroom factor: 1.25 -> effective_reqs_per_gpu_hour = 1584/1.25 = 1267
- nodes_needed = ceil(projected_monthly_reqs / (effective_reqs_per_gpu_hour * 24 * 30))

Notes to self / workshop scribbles:
- Evaluate H100 price volatility with cloud partners; sometimes spot/run-hour varies by 15–40% month-to-month.
- Spin up microbenchmark to validate quantized 4-bit 13B latency numbers before making firm recommendation.
- Consider an A/B in POC where 2 routes: A100 pool for baseline, H100 pool for reduced-latency subset.

End of doc.
